# Goosnav Animation Assistant

Default format: Reels (portrait 9:16, 1080 × 1920). Use landscape only when requested. Frame characters large and centered, minimize negative space, balance top/bottom and left/right margins, and preserve the complete intended pose and action without accidental cropping. Use body fits with 5% padding for wides and face/upper-torso framing for close-ups; inspect the rendered images at action extremes.

Pose and gaze matter as much as framing. Use logical eyelines and body orientation, stable neck/head tilt and body roll, and believable hands, grips and prop contact. Reading, camera address and motivated look-away beats are legitimate; every character need not always face a partner. VIEW actual PNGs at rest, during speaking turns, at action extremes and on both sides of cuts, then fix unintended away-facing characters or sharply backward/sideways heads. composition.poseReview in /AGENTS.md and agentInstructions() gives the full checks and the scoped reset / one-shot align controls. Metadata and successful commands do not establish pose quality.

Default dialogue coverage: wide with both characters → A close-up speaking → B close-up speaking → return wide for the reaction/payoff. Create one sequence export. A 2% zoom is not a new shot. Close-ups emphasize the speaking face and upper torso; do not body-fit every shot. Preserve script order and local actor identity, and compare rendered contact sheets at each cut. Read inspectDocument/validate coverage warnings and revise accidental near-duplicate cuts. Adapt this pattern to the script or explicit user shot list. Example: /examples/dialogue-coverage.json.

Default task for an agent: develop or use the user’s script, compose creative and drawable scenes, inspect real rendered previews, export the reference MP4 AND its matching JSON, and verify delivery to the user’s cloud/computer folder (save locally when unspecified). Specific user instructions override this default. Full operating directions are below and at /AGENTS.md.

Local, deterministic animation authoring with editable scene/sequence JSON and real rendered image feedback.

- Default operating directions: /AGENTS.md
- Visual agent workspace: /agent.html
- Browser ES module: /agent-api.mjs
- API contracts and review workflow: /docs/agents.md
- Multi-shot contract: /docs/sequence.md
- Three-shot example: /examples/three-shot-sequence.json
- Human animation editor: /
- Production reference/artwork/animation pipeline: /pipeline.mjs

Start by reading /AGENTS.md. Import /agent-api.mjs and call agentInstructions() for the same workflow, then capabilities() for the current models, enums, actions, channel ranges and limits. inspectDocument(text) validates without generating speech. editDocument(text, operations) applies atomic JSON-pointer set operations. previewDocument(text, options) returns actual PNG data URLs, frame/shot/drawing identity and measured composition diagnostics. frameDocument(text, options) fits a front camera to posed model geometry while preserving actor and speaker identity.

On /agent.html, window.animationAgent exposes a stateful isolated workspace. Commands: instructions, help, status, validate, preview, patch, frame, reset, align, exportJSON, cancel. Example: await animationAgent.command('preview {"maxDimension":384}'). Use align {"actors":[0,1],"target":"partner","scope":"key","time":0} for one-shot automatic gaze; camera and world-point targets are available, and turnBody defaults to true to reduce neck strain. Use reset {"target":"actor:0","section":"head","scope":"timeline"} to clear only head offsets across the animation and extra dialogue head turns while retaining held pose/expression. Reset defaults to scene scope (base only); key scope resets a pose at time. Alignment does not lock later gaze. Read /AGENTS.md and capabilities() before choosing targets and scopes. The visible Commands panel uses the same API. This is an app command language; it does not execute shell commands or JavaScript.

Review loop: inspect -> render rest/speaking/action/cut samples -> VIEW the returned PNG images -> correct pose, gaze and composition -> render the same samples -> compare -> inspect exported reference frames before delivery. Head visibility and bounds assist review but cannot establish artistic quality. Do not infer that an image was reviewed merely because its metadata was read.

No AI service, API key or model subscription is required. Image rendering needs a browser with WebGL. Speech is generated locally. Preview results are bounded to 12 images, a 1024-pixel long edge per image and one optional contact sheet. The human editor changes only when its Open in editor action is used or JSON is imported there.
